All three clauses are met for each. 1. None uses an untyped bag. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. 2. Identity hooks come after caller props. Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow sets data-presentation-two-way. Callers cannot override any of these. 3. Kit-only props stay off the DOM. id, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out, so the spread rest holds only data-* attributes. The guidance says typed primitives that apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because BoxProps is not the full motion.div prop type. engineering-tests-wait-on-stateengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passNo delivered test opens Playwright itself. A search of tests/ for chromium, playwright, waitForTimeout and sleep finds only a &#39;playwright&#39; dependency-name string in scaffold.test.ts. The browser-driving tests run the delivered verify and inspect scripts as subprocesses through helpers.run, which uses spawnSync. spawnSync blocks until the process exits, so the tests assert on finished output, not after a sleep. Inside the scripts, the step-advance and step-assert waits poll observable state. In verify, waitForIndex polls data-step-index every 50 ms up to STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, and the per-step title and caption are read only after that poll succeeds. In inspect, page.waitForFunction auto-waits until data-step-index equals the target step. Capture is then gated on waitUntilStable, which polls entity geometry until it stops changing. The only timer in the test code is E2E-002&#39;s waitFor helper, a deadline-bounded 100 ms poll on a predicate (preview process alive, &#39;preview ready at&#39; in output, or process gone). That is a polling wait on observable state, not a fixed sleep. Judges A and B match this. Judge C points to `page.waitForTimeout(options.settle)` in inspect, but that does not decide the criterion. That delay is the helper&#39;s user-configurable settle interval, which the INT-002 test checks is honored. It runs only after waitForFunction has already confirmed the step index, so it is not a fixed wait before asserting the step. The capture is still gated by geometry-stability polling. INT-002 also shows a `--settle 0` capture is byte-identical to the default capture, so correctness rests on the state polls, not on the delay. The browser-driving tests run the delivered verify and inspect scripts as subprocesses through helpers.run, which uses spawnSync. spawnSync blocks until the process exits, so the tests assert on finished output, not after a sleep. Inside the scripts, the step-advance and step-assert waits poll observable state. In verify, waitForIndex polls data-step-index every 50 ms up to STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, and the per-step title and caption are read only after that poll succeeds. In inspect, page.waitForFunction auto-waits until data-step-index equals the target step. Capture is then gated on waitUntilStable, which polls entity geometry until it stops changing. The only timer in the test code is E2E-002&#39;s waitFor helper, a deadline-bounded 100 ms poll on a predicate (preview process alive, &#39;preview ready at&#39; in output, or process gone). That is a polling wait on observable state, not a fixed sleep. Judges A and B match this. Judge C points to `page.waitForTimeout(options.settle)` in inspect, but that does not decide the criterion. That delay is the helper&#39;s user-configurable settle interval, which the INT-002 test checks is honored. It runs only after waitForFunction has already confirmed the step index, so it is not a fixed wait before asserting the step. The capture is still gated by geometry-stability polling. INT-002 also shows a `--settle 0` capture is byte-identical to the default capture, so correctness rests on the state polls, not on the delay. source_audits{"demo-integration":[[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Talk.tsx renders the kit&#39;s Presentation with title, steps and initialMode. The shared Scene (Diagram) is typed with the kit&#39;s SceneProps. It uses the kit&#39;s SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Arrow and the other node primitives. It passes each entity&#39;s catalog id as the node id, and Box and Arrow forward it to layoutId. It uses the kit&#39;s `previous` prop to decide Appear wrapping. It does not reimplement layout, motion or stage mechanics. Every step sets Scene: Diagram.","evidence":["Talk.tsx imports Presentation from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39; and renders it with title, steps={STEPS} and initialMode=&quot;browse&quot;.","scene.tsx Diagram({payload, previous}: SceneProps&lt;DiagramState&gt;) returns &lt;SceneLayer&gt;, wrapping ids that are new relative to previous in &lt;Appear&gt; and leaving continuing ids in a Fra…","scene.tsx renderEntity maps entity kinds to kit Box/Label/SymbolChip/Arrow/Frame/Emphasis with id={id}.","Box.tsx and Arrow.tsx set layoutId={id} and layout on a motion.div.","All nine step modules set Scene: Diagram."],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/scene.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SceneLayer.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx","src/presentation-kit/index.ts","src/presentation-kit/types.ts"],"marker":""},{"id":"demo-stable-identity-and-grouping","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The fixture&#39;s grouped-steps requirement is that adjacent steps sharing a scene group and the same scene component update the existing scene instance. Stage builds sceneKey from `group:${step.groupKey}` when groupKey is set and from `step:${step.id}` otherwise, and it keys the motion.div on that. None of the nine step modules sets groupKey, and each has a distinct id. Every step therefore gets a different key. I checked each one. None types its props as an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;. Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip declare named interfaces with explicit field types. They extend DataProps, which is the template-literal index signature { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined }, so extra pass-through props are limited to typed data-* attributes. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. This is typed, but it is narrower than the full rendered-element props: the primitives do not accept aria-* or event props. I treated that as a design choice, since the requirement fails an untyped bag and these are not one. On identity hooks, each of the six node primitives spreads {...data} first on the motion.div. A caller&#39;s data-presentation-* value therefore cannot override them. Appear and SceneLayer spread no caller props, and their data-presentation-appear and data-presentation-layer hooks are fixed. On every step, diagnose() in scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs collects all visible elements that have their own text, plus the chrome that matches &#39;button, a[href], [data-presentation-progress-dot]&#39;. That includes the textless progress-dot buttons that Footer.tsx renders. It compares the intersection of every pair, skipping only pairs where one element contains the other or both sit inside a marked allow-overlap subtree. For each collision of at least 16px² it pushes `step N: overlap between &quot;A&quot; and &quot;B&quot;`, and main() prints these as advisory `warning:` lines while the exit code stays 0. labelOf names each element by its visible text. A textless progress dot is named &#39;progress dot&#39;, which is a plain-words form of its stable data-presentation-progress-dot hook. Other textless chrome gets its aria-label. INT-002 has two focused tests. The first runs fixture-collision, where unmarked AAAA/BBBB labels overlap, and asserts a &#39;warning: step 1: overlap&#39; line. The second runs fixture-chrome-overlap, where CSS moves the progress dots over the step title, and asserts a step-1 overlap warning that names &#39;progress dot&#39;. Judge A&#39;s and Judge C&#39;s pass reasons are confirmed by these lines. Judge B&#39;s reason does not decide the criterion. The guidance accepts a stable hook as the identifier for an element without visible text. It rejects only an empty string, a bare tag name, or a generic label such as &#39;element&#39;. &#39;progress dot&#39; is none of those. It names the progress-dot chrome hook that a reader can find on the page. The guidance does not require using the aria-label in preference to a hook, or telling one sibling dot from another.","evidence":["scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:73-92: chromeSelector includes button, a[href], [data-presentation-progress-dot]. After the deadline it stops the process group and throws. 2. The preview starts only after the build finishes. verify.mjs awaits runBuild(root, log) before it calls startPreview. runBuild resolves only on the build child&#39;s exit with code 0. inspect also awaits runBuild before startPreview; with --skip-build it runs no build at all, so no build is running while the preview starts. 3. The ready-URL clause does not apply. Readiness is an HTTP fetch probe, and the printed output is only kept as a tail for error messages. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C&#39;s reason is that the awaited fetch has no abort signal. The criterion asks for a timeout on every readiness wait, and this wait loop has a hard deadline with cleanup. All three clauses are met for each. 1. None uses an untyped bag. The six node primitives declare typed interfaces that extend DataProps, which is the template-literal type { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined } and not Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. 2. Identity hooks come after caller props. Each node primitive spreads {...data} first on motion.div, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id. Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow sets data-presentation-two-way. Callers cannot override any of these. 3. Kit-only props stay off the DOM. id, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out, so the spread rest holds only data-* attributes. The guidance says typed primitives that apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because BoxProps is not the full motion.div prop type. Browser runs happen only through verify or inspect subprocesses, which tests launch with run() or spawn and then assert on exit status and output. The one in-test wait is E2E-002&#39;s waitFor helper. It polls a predicate on observable state (a preview process exists, or the output contains &#39;preview ready at&#39;) every 100 ms until a deadline, so it is not a fixed sleep. No test calls waitForTimeout or sleep. Inside inspect, the browser waits on state before capturing: waitForFunction polls data-step-index, then waitUntilStable polls entity geometry. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because INT-002 calls inspect with --settle 1500 and inspect runs page.waitForTimeout(options.settle). That settle interval is a configurable inspect-script option. The INT-002 test is checking that the option is honoured (&#39;configured settle 1500ms&#39;, waited &gt;= 1500), not sleeping in place of a state wait. In the script it also comes after the step-index wait. Every preview-readiness wait is bounded. startPreview in both the repo and bootstrap preview.mjs loops only while Date.now() &lt; deadline, where the deadline is now + READY_TIMEOUT_MS (30 000 ms). After the deadline it stops the process group and throws. 2. The preview starts only after the build finishes. verify.mjs awaits runBuild(root, log) before it calls startPreview. runBuild resolves only on the build child&#39;s exit with code 0. inspect also awaits runBuild before startPreview; with --skip-build it runs no build at all, so no build is running while the preview starts. 3. The ready-URL clause does not apply. Readiness is an HTTP fetch probe, and the printed output is only kept as a tail for error messages. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C&#39;s reason is that the awaited fetch has no abort signal. The criterion asks for a timeout on every readiness wait, and this wait loop has a hard deadline with cleanup. C&#39;s case needs a server that accepts the connection and never answers, which is a hypothetical that neither the requirement nor the guidance names. It does not show the readiness wait is unbounded for the behaviour the candidate produces.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs:6 READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000; lines 66-80 run a deadline loop with a fetch probe, then stopProcessGroup and throw &#39;not ready ... within READY_TIMEOUT_MS ms&#39;","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs:66-80 is the same bounded loop in the bootstrap copy","scripts/lib/preview.mjs:27-37 runBuild resolves only on exit code 0","scripts/verify.mjs:127-131 awaits runBuild before startPreview(root, await findFreePort())","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:157-159 runs `if (!options.skipBuild) await runBuild(...)` before startPreview","Output is only kept in outputTail (preview.mjs:53-58); it is never parsed for readiness"],"citations":[{"path":"scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":26,"end_line":81},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","start_line":44,"end_line":81},{"path":"scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":126,"end_line":133},{"path":"scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":157,"end_line":160},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","start_line":126,"end_line":133},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","start_line":157,"end_line":160}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"engineering-typed-kit-primitives","verdict":"pass","rationale":"index.ts exports eight public scene primitives: Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip, Appear and SceneLayer. All three clauses are met for each. 1. None uses an untyped bag. The six node primitives declare typed interfaces that extend DataProps, which is the template-literal type { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined } and not Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;. Appear and SceneLayer take only { children?: ReactNode }. 2. Identity hooks come after caller props. Each node primitive spreads {...data} first on motion.div, then sets layoutId={id}, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id. Box also sets data-presentation-emphasis, and Arrow sets data-presentation-two-way. Callers cannot override any of these. 3. Kit-only props stay off the DOM. id, geometry, icon, emphasized, twoWay, x, y, length and angle are destructured out, so the spread rest holds only data-* attributes. The guidance says typed primitives that apply hooks after caller props and strip kit-only props pass. Judges A and B pass; I rule pass. Judge C fails it because BoxProps is not the full motion.div prop type. The guidance&#39;s fail condition is an untyped bag such as Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;, and DataProps plus explicit typed fields is not one, so C&#39;s observation does not decide the requirement.","evidence":["src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts:11 DataProps = { [key: `data-${string}`]: string | undefined }","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx:7-29 BoxProps is a typed interface; {...data} comes first, then layoutId, data-presentation-node/id/emphasis; icon and emphasized are destructured","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx:20-41 x, y, length, angle and twoWay are destructured; hooks are set after {...data}","Label.tsx, Frame.tsx, Emphasis.tsx and SymbolChip.tsx use the same ordering","Appear.tsx:9-12 and SceneLayer.tsx:8-10 accept only children and spread no caller props"],"citations":[{"path":"src/presentation-kit/index.ts","start_line":8,"end_line":15},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/shared.ts","start_line":10,"end_line":11},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","start_line":7,"end_line":35},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","start_line":6,"end_line":44},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","start_line":6,"end_line":30},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","start_line":6,"end_line":30},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Emphasis.tsx","start_line":6,"end_line":31},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","start_line":7,"end_line":33},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/Appear.tsx","start_line":9,"end_line":22},{"path":"src/presentation-kit/nodes/SceneLayer.tsx","start_line":8,"end_line":14}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"pass","rationale":"No delivered test opens Playwright itself. The browser-driving tests run the delivered verify and inspect scripts as subprocesses through helpers.run, which uses spawnSync. spawnSync blocks until the process exits, so the tests assert on finished output, not after a sleep. Inside the scripts, the step-advance and step-assert waits poll observable state. In verify, waitForIndex polls data-step-index every 50 ms up to STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, and the per-step title and caption are read only after that poll succeeds. In inspect, page.waitForFunction auto-waits until data-step-index equals the target step. Capture is then gated on waitUntilStable, which polls entity geometry until it stops changing. The only timer in the test code is E2E-002&#39;s waitFor helper, a deadline-bounded 100 ms poll on a predicate (preview process alive, &#39;preview ready at&#39; in output, or process gone). That is a polling wait on observable state, not a fixed sleep. Judges A and B match this. Judge C points to `page.waitForTimeout(options.settle)` in inspect, but that does not decide the criterion. That delay is the helper&#39;s user-configurable settle interval, which the INT-002 test checks is honored. It runs only after waitForFunction has already confirmed the step index, so it is not a fixed wait before asserting the step. The capture is still gated by geometry-stability polling. INT-002 also shows a `--settle 0` capture is byte-identical to the default capture, so correctness rests on the state polls, not on the delay.
